subtopics.title: Why Nations Trade — Absolute and Comparative Advantage

questions.question: The SUPPLY-side reasons for international trade include:
options: Differences in natural resources, labour and skills, capital and technology, and climate
The fact that all countries produce the same goods

questions.question: COMPARATIVE advantage tells a country to specialise where:
options: Its output per worker is highest in absolute terms
Its opportunity cost is lowest — where producing the good costs it least in other goods forgone

questions.question: With the same resources, South Africa can make 80 citrus or 20 electronics; South Korea 100 citrus or 200 electronics. A ton of electronics costs each country, in citrus:
options: South Africa half a ton, Korea four tons
South Africa four tons, Korea half a ton — so Korea should specialise in electronics and South Africa in citrus

questions.question: Even though Korea is absolutely better at BOTH goods, trade still benefits both countries because:
options: Absolute advantage is all that matters
Specialising by lowest opportunity cost and trading between the two cost ratios lets both consume beyond their own production frontiers

questions.question: A foreign visitor's spending at a Cape Town hotel is recorded as:
options: A service export on the current account, because their money flows in
Direct investment on the financial account

questions.question: A foreign carmaker building a plant in South Africa versus a foreign fund buying our bonds are, respectively:
options: Direct investment and portfolio investment, both on the financial account
A service import and a merchandise export

questions.question: Portfolio investment earns the nickname HOT MONEY because:
options: It may only be invested in the energy sector
Purchases of shares and bonds can be reversed at the click of a screen and leave in an afternoon
It is prohibited under exchange control

questions.question: The role of the official gold and foreign-exchange reserves in the statement is to:
options: Act as the shock absorber that rises or falls so the whole balance of payments balances

subtopics.title: The Foreign Exchange Market and How the Rand Is Priced

questions.question: The DEMAND for dollars in the South African market comes from:
options: Importers of fuel and electronics, residents touring abroad, firms servicing dollar debt and residents buying foreign shares
Foreign buyers of our coal and citrus
Tourists arriving at Cape Town International
Foreign funds buying our government bonds

questions.question: A drought forces heavy wheat imports. On the diagram for dollars:
options: Supply shifts right and the rand appreciates
Demand shifts right, the rand price of a dollar rises, and the rand depreciates
Demand shifts left and the rand firms

questions.question: The words DEVALUATION and REVALUATION are correctly used for:
options: Any daily movement of the rand
Deliberate resets of the rate by a government operating a fixed exchange rate

questions.question: The trade-off between floating and fixed systems is that:
options: Floating gives certainty while fixed absorbs shocks
Floating absorbs shocks and frees the central bank to fight inflation but is volatile; fixing gives certainty but eats reserves and invites speculative attack

questions.question: Under a floating rate, a persistent deficit begins correcting automatically because:
options: Excess demand for foreign currency slides the rand down, making exports bargains abroad and imports dear at home
The WTO fines the deficit country

questions.question: The cost of the exchange-rate correction channel is:
options: Imported inflation — dearer fuel, machinery and food — and a lag before export volumes respond

questions.question: Correcting a deficit through contractionary demand management works because:
options: Imports are bought out of income, so cooling total spending shrinks the import bill — at the cost of growth and jobs

questions.question: "Diagnosis before prescription" in a disequilibrium essay means:
options: Apply all four channels simultaneously in every case
Match the tool to the cause — an overvalued currency wants exchange-rate adjustment; an overheated economy wants demand restraint

questions.question: Karabo brings vegetables for both plates and Elsa brings bread for both because:
options: Each doing what wastes least effort leaves every braai eating better than either household could alone

questions.question: Even when Elsa is better at BOTH gardening and baking, she still gains from the trade because:
options: An hour in the garden costs Elsa two loaves but costs Karabo almost nothing — her gardening hour is expensive to her, so she should pour it into the bakery

questions.question: "Countries are Karabo and Elsa with anthems" means:
options: Nations, like the two gardeners, gain by doing what costs them least and trading for the rest

questions.question: The snag at the garden gate — Elsa will not accept vegetable vouchers forever — introduces:
options: The question of whose money settles the deal — the foreign exchange problem

subtopics.title: The Rand Has a Price Tag Too

questions.question: Queueing to SELL dollars for rands you would find:
options: The coal exporter paid by India, citrus farmers paid by Europe, arriving tourists, and foreign funds buying our bonds
The fuel importer and the electronics chain
A pension fund buying American shares

questions.question: A ratings downgrade that makes foreign funds dump our bonds moves the rand by:
options: Filling the sell-dollar queue, so the rand firms
Emptying the sell queue and swelling the buy queue, so the rand weakens sharply

questions.question: A record citrus harvest sold into European supermarkets:
options: Weakens the rand by raising imports
Has no effect on the currency
Streams export dollars into the sell queue, so the rand firms

questions.question: "Floating is bumpy but honest; fixed is calm until it snaps" captures the idea that:
options: South Africa pegs the rand to the dollar
Floating rates are set by the Reserve Bank each morning
A floating rate shows the queues' verdict daily with volatility, while a defended peg looks stable until speculators bet the defence must crack

subtopics.title: When the Family Spends More Than It Earns

questions.question: The exercise book's earning and spending pages, its covering page, and the envelope behind the cupboard stand for:
options: The current account, the financial account, and the official reserves
The trade balance, the budget and the repo rate

questions.question: The lending relative who starts attaching conditions represents:
options: The IMF — the lender of last approach, whose conditions are as unwelcome in a cabinet meeting as across a kitchen table

questions.question: The depreciating rand performs which family cure automatically?
options: Making the family's services cheaper to outsiders — exports become bargains and imports become luxuries
Tightening the belt through higher interest rates

questions.question: Fitting the cure to the disease means:
options: Every deficit needs all four cures at once
A family that simply overspends needs the belt — demand restraint — while one whose prices are uncompetitive needs the price cut — depreciation
